fields.h1: Build a Consent Form That Records Exactly What Was Signed
fields.hero_description: Describe what people are agreeing to. Emergent builds the consent form, collects each signature on any device and keeps every record in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Consent Form Has to Do
fields.features_subheading: Each one answers a question asked later: what did this person read, which version did they sign, did they withdraw?
fields.feature_1:
Key information before the fine print

Open each form with a short summary of the purpose, the time it takes and the main risks. The detailed sections come next, and the signature field waits below all of them.
fields.feature_2:
Initials beside the risks that matter

Ask for initials next to any risk that needs its own moment, such as dry socket after an extraction. The signer cannot submit the form until every initial box has been filled in.
fields.feature_3:
Every signature tied to its version

Keep the consent text as numbered versions. Each signature saves the version number and the time. A record from March then shows the exact wording that participant agreed to.
fields.feature_4:
Withdrawal that takes one link

Give every signer a link to withdraw. The record stays in the table, marked withdrawn with the date, and the study coordinator or clinic manager gets an email the same minute.
fields.feature_5:
A signed copy for every signer

Send each signer a PDF of the form with their signature and the date on it. Keep the same copy in your own database next to their answers, ready for the day someone audits.
fields.feature_6:
Source code you can take anywhere

Export the full source of the form and its signature records to your GitHub. A developer can then host it on your own servers or connect it to a study system you already run.

fields.usecase_heading: Consent Forms for Every Kind of Signer
fields.tab_content_1:
Re-consent goes out the day a new version is approved

Version 4 of the sleep study text adds a new risk. Once the IRB approves it, the 12 participants who signed version 3 each get a link to read the change and sign again. The coordinator sees who has re-signed, and the table shows the version behind every signature.
fields.tab_content_2:
Read at home, two days before the appointment

Two days before an extraction, the patient gets an email with the consent form. Risks such as dry socket are written in plain words, with initials beside each before the signature. At the front desk, staff see that 12 of tomorrow's 14 patients have signed.
fields.tab_content_3:
A parent's permission and the child's own assent

Parents sign first, on the full permission form for the youth sleep study. Their 11-year-old then gets a shorter assent page in plain words, with a yes button and a no button. The study record holds both signatures, and a no from the child stops enrollment.
fields.tab_content_4:
Let each signer choose English or Spanish

Participants choose a language on the first screen of the community health study. The Spanish text is the one the IRB approved, not a machine translation. This month the coordinator counts 41 Spanish consents, and each signer gets a copy in the language they chose.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work happens before the first field: deciding who signs, what they read first and how they change their mind later.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Adults sign for themselves. Minors need a parent's permission and, in research, their own assent once they are old enough to give it. Someone who cannot consent may need a legally authorized representative. Give each type of signer a separate path through the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put a short summary first: the purpose, how long participation lasts and the risks most likely to matter to the reader. The federal Common Rule asks research consent to begin with this kind of summary, ahead of the detailed sections.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe the procedures, the foreseeable risks, the expected benefits and any alternatives. Say who sees the information, whom to contact with questions and that declining carries no penalty. Your institution's template usually sets the exact headings for research.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use short sentences and everyday words. Federal research rules require consent information in language the participant understands. Anyone who reads Spanish better than English gets a Spanish version your IRB has approved, never one improvised on the day.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the approved text into the prompt word for word, then say where initials go and the order people sign in. Emergent builds the form and the signature records. Change the wording later by prompting, and the change is saved as a new version.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick who hears about each signature and each withdrawal, by email or in Slack. Send the signer a PDF of what they signed. Federal research rules require that a copy of the signed form goes to the person who signed it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form on a phone as a made-up participant, sign it, then withdraw. Read the PDF and the stored record line by line. Have your IRB or a lawyer review the text before the first real person signs it.

claims_to_source: Under the federal Common Rule, consent information must be in language understandable to the subject, open with a concise presentation of key information, and cover purpose, procedures, risks, benefits, alternatives, confidentiality, contacts and the right to refuse or withdraw without penalty
The Common Rule documents consent with a written form approved by the IRB and signed, including electronically, by the subject or a legally authorized representative, with a copy given to the signer
Research with children needs a parent's permission and, when the child is capable, the child's own assent

Express consent is given in words or in writing, implied consent is given by actions such as rolling up a sleeve for an injection, and informed consent means the person has the information needed to decide
Memorial University's sexual harassment office uses confidentiality, choice and consent as its three C's
Planned Parenthood's FRIES model says consent is freely given, reversible, informed, enthusiastic and specific
